listening.title: Corporate training webinar — new expense card tiers and rollover rules
listening.speaker: Single HR presenter
listening.transcript: PRESENTER: Thanks for joining this short training on the new corporate card system, rolling out company-wide starting the first of next month. Every employee will be assigned to one of three card tiers based on role, not seniority — this is a common point of confusion, since some newer employees in client-facing roles will actually receive a higher tier than long-tenured staff in internal roles. Tier A, for roles involving regular client travel, carries a monthly limit of $2,000, and unused amounts roll over up to a maximum accumulated balance of $3,000 — so if you spend nothing one month, you don't simply gain another $2,000 on top, you're capped at that $3,000 ceiling regardless of how many months you save. Tier B, for occasional travel roles, has a $900 monthly limit with no rollover at all; whatever isn't used resets to zero at the start of each month. Tier C, for non-travel roles, isn't a monthly allowance at all, but rather a $500 per-quarter limit intended mainly for client meals and small local expenses, and this one does roll over fully between quarters within the same calendar year, though it resets to zero every January regardless of what's remaining. Now, here's an important exception: regardless of your assigned tier, any single purchase over $750 requires pre-approval from your manager through the portal before the charge is made, not after — charges made without that pre-approval, even if they're within your monthly or quarterly limit, will be flagged for mandatory review and may result in personal reimbursement liability if not resolved within five business days. One more note specific to Tier A: because travel bookings often span two calendar months, a hotel or flight booking that begins in one month and is paid in full at booking may count against either month's limit, whichever the traveler selects at the time of booking, but this choice cannot be changed retroactively once submitted. Please direct questions to the finance help desk, not your manager, since managers only handle pre-approvals, not general policy questions.

questions.label: Question 1
questions.question: What determines an employee's card tier?
options: Seniority within the company
Role, not seniority
Department budget size
Length of time with the company
questions.explanation: The presenter states tiers are assigned 'based on role, not seniority.'

questions.label: Question 2
questions.question: Why does the presenter call the tier system 'a common point of confusion'?
options: Because the tiers change every month
Because some newer client-facing employees may receive a higher tier than long-tenured internal staff
Because tiers are assigned randomly
Because tier names are not standardized across departments
questions.explanation: The presenter notes newer client-facing employees 'will actually receive a higher tier than long-tenured staff in internal roles.'

questions.label: Question 3
questions.question: What is the monthly limit for Tier A?
questions.explanation: Tier A 'carries a monthly limit of $2,000.'

questions.label: Question 4
questions.question: What is the maximum accumulated rollover balance for Tier A?
questions.explanation: Unused Tier A amounts roll over 'up to a maximum accumulated balance of $3,000.'

questions.label: Question 5
questions.question: If a Tier A employee spends nothing for two consecutive months, how much will they have available in month three?
options: $4,000, since $2,000 accumulates each month
$6,000, the full sum of three months
$3,000, the capped ceiling regardless of savings
$2,000, since rollover doesn't apply after two months
questions.explanation: The presenter explicitly says the balance is 'capped at that $3,000 ceiling regardless of how many months you save.'

questions.label: Question 6
questions.question: What is the monthly limit for Tier B?
questions.explanation: Tier B 'has a $900 monthly limit.'

questions.label: Question 7
questions.question: Does Tier B allow any rollover?
options: Yes, up to $3,000
Yes, but only for one month
No, unused amounts reset to zero each month
Yes, fully, like Tier C
questions.explanation: Tier B has 'no rollover at all; whatever isn't used resets to zero at the start of each month.'

questions.label: Question 8
questions.question: How is Tier C structured differently from Tiers A and B?
options: It has no limit at all
It is a per-quarter limit rather than a monthly allowance
It only applies to travel expenses
It requires pre-approval for every purchase
questions.explanation: Tier C 'isn't a monthly allowance at all, but rather a $500 per-quarter limit.'

questions.label: Question 9
questions.question: Does Tier C's balance roll over between quarters?
options: No, it resets every quarter
Yes, fully between quarters within the same calendar year, but resets every January
Yes, indefinitely with no annual reset
Only if pre-approved by a manager
questions.explanation: Tier C 'roll[s] over fully between quarters within the same calendar year, though it resets to zero every January.'

questions.label: Question 10
questions.question: If a Tier C employee accumulates $1,200 by the end of Q3 but doesn't spend it, what happens to that balance in January?
options: It carries over into the new year automatically
It resets to zero regardless of the remaining balance
Half of it carries over
It converts to Tier B limits
questions.explanation: Tier C 'resets to zero every January regardless of what's remaining,' even with accumulated unspent funds.

questions.label: Question 11
questions.question: What purchase amount triggers the mandatory pre-approval rule, regardless of tier?
questions.explanation: The presenter says 'any single purchase over $750 requires pre-approval from your manager.'

questions.label: Question 12
questions.question: What happens if an employee makes a $900 purchase within their monthly limit but without required pre-approval?
options: Nothing, since it's within the limit
It is automatically declined by the card
It will be flagged for mandatory review and may result in personal reimbursement liability if unresolved within five business days
The employee's tier is downgraded immediately
questions.explanation: The presenter warns that charges made without pre-approval, 'even if they're within your monthly or quarterly limit,' will be flagged and may create personal liability if unresolved in five business days.

questions.label: Question 13
questions.question: When must pre-approval be obtained for a purchase over $750?
options: Within 24 hours after the charge
Before the charge is made
Within five business days after the charge
At the end of the quarter
questions.explanation: Pre-approval is required 'before the charge is made, not after.'

questions.label: Question 14
questions.question: For a Tier A travel booking spanning two months, who decides which month's limit it counts against?
options: The manager, at the time of pre-approval
The finance help desk, after the trip
The traveler, at the time of booking, and this choice cannot be changed later
It automatically counts against the earlier month
questions.explanation: The traveler selects which month it counts against 'at the time of booking, but this choice cannot be changed retroactively.'

questions.label: Question 15
questions.question: A Tier A employee books a $1,600 flight in March for an April trip, selecting it to count against March's limit, and separately wants to make an $800 hotel purchase in March. Based on the announcement, what must this employee do regarding the hotel purchase, and who should they contact if they have a general question about how the tier system works overall?
options: Get manager pre-approval for the hotel since it exceeds $750, and direct general policy questions to the finance help desk, not the manager
No pre-approval is needed for the hotel since the flight already used the March limit; general questions go to the manager
Get pre-approval for both the flight and hotel from the finance help desk, since both exceed $750
No action needed for either purchase since the employee is Tier A; policy questions go to the finance help desk
questions.explanation: The $800 hotel charge exceeds the $750 pre-approval threshold regardless of tier or remaining balance, requiring manager pre-approval before the charge; general policy questions are directed to the finance help desk, since managers only handle pre-approvals.

reading.title: Municipal utility notice — tiered water rate restructuring and conservation credits
reading.passage:
City of Fairhaven Water Utility — Rate Restructuring Notice

Beginning with the billing cycle starting January 1, residential water rates will shift from a single flat rate to a four-tier consumption model, intended to encourage conservation while keeping basic usage affordable. Tier 1 covers the first 4,000 gallons used per month and is billed at the current rate of $0.004 per gallon, unchanged from today. Tier 2 covers usage from 4,001 to 8,000 gallons and is billed at $0.006 per gallon — note that this rate applies only to the gallons within that range, not retroactively to the entire bill, so a household using 6,000 gallons pays the Tier 1 rate on the first 4,000 gallons and the Tier 2 rate only on the remaining 2,000.

Tier 3 covers 8,001 to 15,000 gallons at $0.009 per gallon, and Tier 4 covers any usage above 15,000 gallons at $0.014 per gallon, more than triple the base rate, intended primarily to discourage non-essential high-volume use such as excessive landscape irrigation.

Households that reduce their consumption by at least 15% compared to the same month last year qualify for a conservation credit equal to 10% of that month's total bill, applied automatically the following billing cycle; however, this credit is only available to households whose usage last year was already at or below 10,000 gallons for that month, since the credit program is designed to reward households with already-modest usage rather than those cutting back from very high baselines.

Households with a documented medical necessity for higher water use, such as certain home dialysis equipment, may apply for a Tier 1 rate extension covering up to 10,000 gallons monthly instead of the standard 4,000-gallon threshold, but this exemption must be renewed annually with updated medical documentation and does not apply retroactively to bills issued before the exemption is approved.

Customers disputing a bill under the new structure have 45 days from the billing date to file an appeal, but appeals filed after usage has already been paid in full will only be eligible for a bill credit toward a future statement, not a direct refund, unless the dispute involves a confirmed meter malfunction, in which case a direct refund remains available regardless of payment status.

questions.label: Question 1
questions.question: What billing model is replacing the flat rate?
options: A two-tier model
A three-tier model
A four-tier consumption model
A fully usage-independent flat fee
questions.explanation: Rates will shift 'from a single flat rate to a four-tier consumption model.'

questions.label: Question 2
questions.question: What is the rate for Tier 1 usage?
options: $0.004 per gallon
$0.006 per gallon
$0.009 per gallon
$0.014 per gallon
questions.explanation: Tier 1 is 'billed at the current rate of $0.004 per gallon, unchanged from today.'

questions.label: Question 3
questions.question: A household uses 6,000 gallons in a month. How is their bill calculated?
options: All 6,000 gallons at the Tier 2 rate
The first 4,000 gallons at Tier 1 rate, and the remaining 2,000 at Tier 2 rate
All 6,000 gallons at the Tier 1 rate
6,000 gallons split evenly between all four tiers
questions.explanation: The notice explains this exact example: 'a household using 6,000 gallons pays the Tier 1 rate on the first 4,000 gallons and the Tier 2 rate only on the remaining 2,000.'

questions.label: Question 4
questions.question: What gallon range does Tier 3 cover?
options: 0 to 4,000 gallons
4,001 to 8,000 gallons
8,001 to 15,000 gallons
Above 15,000 gallons
questions.explanation: Tier 3 'covers 8,001 to 15,000 gallons.'

questions.label: Question 5
questions.question: What is notable about the Tier 4 rate compared to the base rate?
options: It is exactly double the base rate
It is more than triple the base rate
It is the same as Tier 3
It is capped regardless of usage
questions.explanation: The Tier 4 rate of $0.014 is described as 'more than triple the base rate.'

questions.label: Question 6
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Tier 4 rate?
options: To fund new infrastructure exclusively
To discourage non-essential high-volume use such as excessive landscape irrigation
To subsidize Tier 1 households
To phase out residential water service
questions.explanation: Tier 4 is 'intended primarily to discourage non-essential high-volume use such as excessive landscape irrigation.'

questions.label: Question 7
questions.question: What consumption reduction qualifies a household for the conservation credit?
options: Any reduction at all
At least 10%
At least 15% compared to the same month last year
Exactly 20%
questions.explanation: Households must reduce consumption 'by at least 15% compared to the same month last year.'

questions.label: Question 8
questions.question: What is the size of the conservation credit?
options: 5% of that month's bill
10% of that month's total bill
15% of that month's total bill
A flat $10 credit
questions.explanation: Qualifying households receive 'a conservation credit equal to 10% of that month's total bill.'

questions.label: Question 9
questions.question: A household used 12,000 gallons last year and reduces usage by 20% this year. Do they qualify for the conservation credit?
options: Yes, since their reduction exceeds 15%
No, because their prior usage exceeded the 10,000-gallon eligibility threshold
Yes, but only for a partial credit
No, because the credit doesn't apply to any household using more than 4,000 gallons
questions.explanation: The credit is 'only available to households whose usage last year was already at or below 10,000 gallons,' so 12,000 gallons disqualifies them despite the 20% reduction.

questions.label: Question 10
questions.question: Why does the utility restrict the conservation credit to households with modest prior usage?
options: To reduce total administrative costs
Because the program is designed to reward already-modest usage rather than cuts from very high baselines
Because higher-usage households are ineligible for any city programs
Because the credit only applies to Tier 1 customers
questions.explanation: The program 'is designed to reward households with already-modest usage rather than those cutting back from very high baselines.'

questions.label: Question 11
questions.question: What does the medical necessity exemption allow?
options: Unlimited water use at Tier 1 rates
A Tier 1 rate extension covering up to 10,000 gallons monthly instead of 4,000
A complete waiver of all water charges
Automatic enrollment in the conservation credit program
questions.explanation: Qualifying households 'may apply for a Tier 1 rate extension covering up to 10,000 gallons monthly instead of the standard 4,000-gallon threshold.'

questions.label: Question 12
questions.question: Does the medical exemption apply retroactively to past bills?
options: Yes, to any bill issued that year
No, it does not apply retroactively to bills issued before approval
Yes, but only for the current billing cycle
The notice does not address this
questions.explanation: The exemption 'does not apply retroactively to bills issued before the exemption is approved.'

questions.label: Question 13
questions.question: How often must the medical exemption be renewed?
options: Every month
Every quarter
Annually
It is permanent once approved
questions.explanation: The exemption 'must be renewed annually with updated medical documentation.'

questions.label: Question 14
questions.question: How many days does a customer have to file a billing appeal?
options: 15 days
30 days
45 days
60 days
questions.explanation: Customers have '45 days from the billing date to file an appeal.'

questions.label: Question 15
questions.question: A customer paid their bill in full, then discovered a discrepancy and filed an appeal within the 45-day window. It is later confirmed the water meter itself was malfunctioning. Based on the notice, what remedy is this customer entitled to?
options: Only a bill credit toward a future statement, since the bill was already paid
No remedy, since appeals after payment are generally limited to credits
A direct refund, since confirmed meter malfunctions remain eligible for direct refunds regardless of payment status
A partial credit equal to 10%, the same as the conservation credit
questions.explanation: While appeals after payment are normally limited to a bill credit, the notice creates an exception: 'unless the dispute involves a confirmed meter malfunction, in which case a direct refund remains available regardless of payment status.'
